national.title: How to Register Property Sale Deed in India (2026)
national.summary: Master procedure for registering immovable property sale deeds under The Registration Act 1908. Verified guide covering title search, circle rate valuation, stamp duty payment, and Sub-Registrar biometric execution.

steps.title: Verify Property Title and Obtain Encumbrance Certificate
steps.description: Check ownership chain records for at least thirteen to thirty years at the Sub-Registrar office. Obtain a Nil Encumbrance Certificate to confirm the property is free of legal mortgages or disputes.
steps.where: Jurisdictional Sub-Registrar Office or State IGR Portal
steps.calloutText: Never proceed with purchase without reviewing original title deeds and chain documents.

steps.title: Calculate Property Valuation via Circle Rate
steps.description: Determine the minimum government guideline value of the property based on local circle rates or jantasri. The sale deed value cannot be lower than the official circle rate.
steps.where: State IGR Registration Portal or Revenue Office
steps.calloutText: Stamp duty is calculated on whichever is higher: the actual sale price or the government circle rate.

steps.title: Draft the Sale Deed with Legal Covenants
steps.description: Engage an advocate to draft the sale deed including property boundaries, payment schedules, encumbrance indemnities, and handover terms. Ensure all names match Aadhaar and PAN cards.
steps.where: Advocate Office or Legal Drafter Chamber
steps.calloutText: List north, south, east, and west property boundaries accurately in the schedule of property.

steps.title: Pay Stamp Duty and Registration Charges via e-Stamping
steps.description: Purchase e-stamp certificate online or through authorized banks for the required stamp duty amount. Pay the one percent registration fee through state cyber treasury portals.
steps.where: Authorized Bank, e-Stamping Center, or Cyber Treasury Portal
steps.calloutText: E-stamp certificates carry a unique identification number verifiable online by the Sub-Registrar.

steps.title: Book Appointment Slot at Sub-Registrar Office
steps.description: Visit the state registration portal to upload the draft deed and payment challans. Select an appointment date and time slot for physical appearance at the local Sub-Registrar Office.
steps.calloutText: Download and print the appointment acknowledgement slip containing the token number.

steps.title: Present Documents at Sub-Registrar Office
steps.description: Buyer, seller, and two witnesses must arrive at the Sub-Registrar office fifteen minutes before the allotted slot. Submit original deeds, tax receipts, and identity proofs for scrutiny.
steps.calloutText: Both witnesses must be present in person with original government photo identity cards.

steps.title: Complete Biometric Verification and Signatures
steps.description: The Sub-Registrar verifies identities against government databases and records digital photos and fingerprints. Both parties sign the official register in the presence of the officer.

steps.title: Collect Registered Sale Deed and Index II Copy
steps.description: Collect the final registered deed bearing the official registration number, volume, and seal after scanning. Obtain an official Index II copy as conclusive legal proof of ownership.
steps.where: Sub-Registrar Office Delivery Counter or Online Portal
steps.calloutText: Immediately apply for revenue mutation to update property records in municipal or land registries.

documentRequirements.name: Original Draft Sale Deed on Stamp Paper
documentRequirements.description: Legal deed executed between buyer and seller with full schedule of property and consideration details.

documentRequirements.name: Chain of Title Documents and Parent Deed
documentRequirements.description: Original previous sale deeds, allotment letters, or gift deeds establishing the seller legal ownership.

documentRequirements.name: Encumbrance Certificate (EC Form 15 or 16)
documentRequirements.description: Official certificate issued by the Sub-Registrar showing registered transactions on the property for recent decades.

documentRequirements.name: Latest Property Tax and Utility Receipts
documentRequirements.description: Recent municipal property tax assessment receipt and electricity bill showing no outstanding municipal dues.

documentRequirements.name: Aadhaar and PAN Cards of Buyer and Seller
documentRequirements.description: Self-attested photocopies of identity proofs and PAN cards for income tax reporting and biometric verification.

documentRequirements.name: Identity Proofs of Two Adult Witnesses
documentRequirements.description: Aadhaar cards or Voter ID cards of two adult witnesses who will identify the parties before the Sub-Registrar.

documentRequirements.name: Non-Agricultural (NA) Land Conversion Order
documentRequirements.description: Official revenue order permitting use of agricultural land for residential or commercial development.

documentRequirements.name: No Objection Certificate from Housing Society
documentRequirements.description: Letter issued by the cooperative housing society confirming transfer approval and maintenance clearance.

fees.label: State Stamp Duty (National Average 4% to 7%)
fees.notes: Statutory stamp duty calculated as percentage of circle rate or sale price. Amount varies by state.

fees.label: Property Registration Fee (Standard 1%)
fees.notes: Statutory registration charge payable to the Registration Department under The Registration Act 1908.

fees.label: Document Scanning and Computerized Pasting Charges
fees.notes: Administrative fee charged by the Sub-Registrar Office for digital archival and Index II generation.

rejectionReasons.title: Sale Value Declared Below Official Government Circle Rate
rejectionReasons.description: The Sub-Registrar will refuse registration if the property valuation is lower than the minimum statutory circle rate.
rejectionReasons.solution: Revalue the property according to the official circle rate and pay the differential stamp duty.

rejectionReasons.title: Absence of Valid PAN Card or Form 60 for High Value Transfer
rejectionReasons.description: Income tax regulations mandate valid PAN details for property transactions exceeding five lakh rupees.
rejectionReasons.solution: Provide valid PAN cards of buyer and seller or submit duly filled Form 60 declarations.

rejectionReasons.title: Submitting Deed at Incorrect Sub-Registrar Office
rejectionReasons.description: Sale deeds must be registered strictly within the territorial jurisdiction where the property is located.
rejectionReasons.solution: Verify the revenue village and taluka to book an appointment with the correct jurisdictional SRO.

rejectionReasons.title: Short Payment or Invalid e-Stamp Certificate
rejectionReasons.description: Discrepancies in e-stamp certificate numbers or failure to pay the full calculated duty causes immediate suspension.
rejectionReasons.solution: Purchase supplementary e-stamp certificates for the remaining amount before presenting the deed.

rejectionReasons.title: Absence of Two Adult Witnesses with Valid Identity Proofs
rejectionReasons.description: Law requires two independent adult witnesses who know the parties to be physically present.
rejectionReasons.solution: Bring two adult witnesses carrying original Aadhaar cards, Voter IDs, or Passports.

rejectionReasons.title: Existing Undischarged Bank Mortgage or Court Attachment
rejectionReasons.description: Properties with registered financial liens cannot be transferred without formal bank release.
rejectionReasons.solution: Obtain a formal deed of reconveyance or bank release deed before executing the sale.

faqItems.question: Is property registration mandatory under Indian law?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Section 17 of The Registration Act 1908 makes registration mandatory for any transfer of immovable property worth over 100 rupees.

faqItems.question: How is stamp duty calculated for property registration?
faqItems.answer: Stamp duty is calculated as a percentage of the higher value between the actual transaction price and the government circle rate.

faqItems.question: Do female property buyers receive stamp duty concessions?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Several state governments offer a one to two percent reduction in stamp duty when property is registered in a woman name.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between circle rate and market rate?
faqItems.answer: Circle rate is the minimum valuation set by the state government for taxes. Market rate is the negotiated price between buyer and seller.

faqItems.question: Can property be registered online without visiting the Sub-Registrar office?
faqItems.answer: No. While slot booking and duty payments happen online, physical appearance of buyer, seller, and witnesses is legally mandatory for biometrics.

faqItems.question: What is an Encumbrance Certificate and why is it essential?
faqItems.answer: An Encumbrance Certificate shows registered transactions on the property. It confirms the title is unencumbered by prior mortgages or legal attachments.

faqItems.question: What is an Index II copy?
faqItems.answer: Index II is the official document issued by the Sub-Registrar summarizing property details, buyer, seller, stamp duty, and registration date.

faqItems.question: What must I do immediately after registering the sale deed?
faqItems.answer: Apply for property mutation at the local municipal corporation or taluka revenue office to update municipal tax and land records.

GJ.title: How to Register Property Sale Deed in Gujarat (2026)
GJ.summary: Property registration in Gujarat is conducted via the GARVI portal operated by the Inspector General of Registration. Stamp duty is 4.9 percent of the jantasri value or market consideration, and female purchasers receive full exemption from registration fees.
